about: The states and territories of late 1850 (after California's admission on September 9), in four plain groups, for a lesson map. Outlines are Esri's digitization of the 1850 plate in Harper's Atlas of American History (1920), a public-domain map in the Library of Congress (loc.gov/item/32005827). The source classes each area by the law that made it free or slave, in 16 classes; this table replaces those with four. Fact-checked on 11 November 2026 (maps/data/checks/replacement-maps-factcheck-2026-11-11.md).

units.note: Admitted as a free state under the Missouri Compromise of 1820.

units.basis: An 1846 law abolished slavery here but kept the last enslaved people bound to their owners as 'apprentices'. The 1850 census still counted 236 people as enslaved.
Admitted as a free state on September 9, 1850, as part of the Compromise of 1850.

units.note: Includes today's West Virginia, which was part of Virginia until 1863.
Annexed as a slave state in 1845.

Admitted as a slave state under the Missouri Compromise of 1820, although almost all of it lies north of the compromise line. The source map draws the northwest corner, added in 1837, separately; here it is part of the state.

units.name: District of Columbia
units.basis: Slavery was legal here. A law in the Compromise of 1850 banned bringing enslaved people into the District to sell them, starting January 1, 1851. It did not end slavery here.

units.name: Minnesota Territory
units.basis: Organized in 1849. Slavery was banned here.

units.name: Unorganized territory
units.basis: Closed to slavery by the Missouri Compromise of 1820, because it lies north of the compromise line.

units.name: Utah Territory
units.basis: Organized by the Compromise of 1850, which left slavery for the settlers to decide.
units.note: Includes a small area on its eastern edge that the source map draws separately: land north of the Missouri Compromise line that the 1850 act placed in Utah Territory.

units.name: New Mexico Territory
units.basis: Organized by the Compromise of 1850, which left slavery for the settlers to decide.

units.name: Indian Territory
units.basis: Not an organized territory. Slavery was legal among several of the nations moved here in the 1830s.

units.name: Unorganized land given up by Texas
units.basis: Claimed by Texas until 1850. The 1845 resolution that annexed Texas barred slavery in its land north of the Missouri Compromise line. In 1850 it was left outside any organized territory.
